newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MAS accused of falling standards.
newsitem.headline: MAS accused of falling standards.

text.p: National carrier Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) will meet government officials in the next two days to answer accusations of falling standards, a company official said on Monday.

"It's not right for us to say anything more at this juncture as our management is meeting the Transport Ministry in the next two days," the official, who declined to be named, told Reuters by telephone.

Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Sunday that the government had initiated an inquiry into MAS after the local Berita Harian newspaper reported that service was deteriorating, partly due to a lack of pilots and cabin crew.
The national Bernama news agency reported at the weekend that Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik had acknowledged the problem and planned to meet MAS' management.
The MAS official admitted the carrier was short of workers but added that "this is a problem faced by companies all over Malaysia".
"We're reading daily of staff being pinched from one place to another with double pay and what-not," said the official. "We haven't been spared."
Parliamentary opposition leader Lim Kit Siang said on Sunday that salaries and working conditions of MAS pilots and other cabin crew should be reviewed at once.
"The services of MAS has definitely deteriorated in the past year and more, with many flight delays as well as unsatisfactory handling of customer inquiries and complaints," Lim said in a statement.
MAS share price was up five cents at 6.15 ringgit at 0400 GMT.
